dedupe_keys.name: dlr skyscapes aerial image dataset with fine grained road and lane marking annotations

description: DLR-SkyScapes is an aerial image dataset with pixel-level annotations for high-definition mapping of roads and urban infrastructure, for uses from automated driving to infrastructure monitoring. It labels 31 semantic categories, including paved and non-paved roads and parking, bike-ways, sidewalks, entrances, danger areas, buildings, vehicle types, vegetation and 12 types of lane markings such as dash lines, stop lines, crosswalks and zebra zones, and defines benchmarks for dense, lane-marking, category and edge segmentation. The 16 non-overlapping RGB images of 5616 by 3744 pixels were taken by DLR from a helicopter or aircraft with a three-camera DSLR array at about 1,000 m, giving a ground sampling distance of about 13 cm, over urban and partly rural areas with highways and complex traffic in German and other European cities, such as a Munich tunnel scene; it was published at ICCV 2019 by Azimi and co-authors. Coverage is local. The training and validation sets are free to download from the DLR page as a ZIP archive (275 MB), and the test set is kept for an online benchmark; the page images are credited CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 and no separate data licence is stated. Caveats: it has only 16 images from a few flights. It supports automated extraction of road inventories and lane markings for digital twins and condition monitoring of road assets. It complements the DLR highway and urban traffic datasets and is related to the Montréal road assets database.
